decisions.reason: Requiring a randomly distributed commission to appear in NFT attributes does not change how NFT images, covers, or detail media render.
The source does not change which NFT properties, tickets, badges, or access rights follow an NFT after transfer.
The source concerns visibility of a no-code purchase commission and does not change secondary-sale royalty rules.
The metadata visibility change does not alter the required blockchain network or deployment context.
Displaying a distributed commission in NFT attributes does not change whether an owner's NFTs are discoverable in wallet or dashboard views.
The source adds commission visibility to NFT attributes but does not change the NFT's referral-code source, persistence, or display locations.
The possible UI-note revision is conditional on the unresolved ticket behavior and does not necessarily revise the approved FAQ content.
The source requires visibility of the weighted commission outcome but does not change the commission amount, trigger, or recipient-selection mechanics owned by this allocation Requirement.
The source does not necessarily change landing-page copy or layout; its UI-note reference is conditional and unspecified.

Whether a no-code purchase generates a ticket remains unresolved and is already represented by the same-message AMBIGUOUS Event; the commission metadata change does not resolve or modify ticket allocation.
The source concerns randomly distributed commissions from no-code purchases, not commissions paid to the referrer on coded-referral mints.
Commission visibility in NFT attributes has no effect on the landing-page book cover's placement, size, or cropping.
